DLG_STAROSTA_HELLO: Be well, travellers. I am the elder here. Strangers seldom come our way — what brings you?
DLG_STAROSTA_AGAIN: You again? Well, say what you need.
DLG_STAROSTA_ASK_BED: We need a place to sleep.
DLG_STAROSTA_BED: You'll have a bed if you keep the peace. Go to the smith — his hayloft is roomy.
DLG_STAROSTA_NEWS: What news could we have… Our herbalist, Mlava, went to the woods three days ago and came back not herself. Says she saw lights on the marsh.
DLG_TRAVNITSA_HELLO: What do you want, good man? Herbs, or a cure for some ailment?
DLG_TRAVNITSA_ASK_LIGHTS: The elder said you saw lights on the marsh.
DLG_TRAVNITSA_LIGHTS: I did… Blue and cold. They drift over the bog as if searching for someone. Don't go there at night, you hear?
DLG_KUZNETS_HELLO: Well? A horse to shoe or an axe to sharpen? Speak quickly, the forge is cooling.
DLG_KUZNETS_BED: The elder sent you? Fine, the hayloft is behind the forge. Just no fire in there!
DLG_KUZNETS_REST: Hayloft behind the forge, I told you. Get some rest.
DLG_TRAVNITSA_PRESS: You haven't told us everything. Speak plainly — we'll help.
DLG_TRAVNITSA_SECRET: Persistent, aren't you… Very well. The lights are only half the trouble. At the old graveyard a noon wraith walks at midday. Whoever she catches in the heat, she cuts down with her sickle. The sun is her strength; shade hinders her.
DLG_TRAVNITSA_THANKS: Thank you, Mlava. We'll be careful.
DLG_TRAVNITSA_REFUSE: I told you all I know. Strangers shouldn't meddle in our affairs. Go.
DLG_TRAVNITSA_ASK_AGAIN: Remind us about the noon wraith.
DLG_TRAVNITSA_SECRET_AGAIN: At the graveyard, at noon. Keep to the shade and don't linger.
QUEST_KRYSY_STARTED: Elder Ratibor asks us to drive the rats out of the cellar of his house. The reward is in the chest down there.
QUEST_KRYSY_CLEARED: The rats are dead. The reward waits in the chest in the cellar.
QUEST_KRYSY_DONE: The elder's chest is opened, the reward is ours.
DLG_STAROSTA_ASK_WORK: Is there any work for us?
DLG_STAROSTA_WORK: There is, though it's a shameful thing… Rats have bred in the cellar — big as cats, gnawing the grain, not afraid of people. Drive them out — the chest is down there too, and whatever is in it is yours.
DLG_STAROSTA_THANKS: Thank you, you saved us! The chest in the cellar is yours, as agreed.
DLG_TAT_HELLO: What are you staring at? I'm sitting here, bothering nobody. For now.
DLG_TAT_ASK_JOIN: We need people for the road. Will you come?
DLG_TAT_ASK_WHO: You're one of the outlaws, aren't you?
DLG_TAT_WHO_OK: Sharp eyes. I was in the woods with the ataman. Left — I don't like it when they stab their own in the back. Now I'm on my own.
DLG_TAT_WHO_FAIL: What's it to you who I am? Go your way.
DLG_TAT_TERMS: Depends where. If it's the woods where the ataman's band sits — I'm in. He owes me.
DLG_TAT_DEAL: Deal. We'll collect that debt together.
DLG_TAT_JOINED: Good. Just don't forget my share.
DLG_YARYY_HELLO: Ha! Travellers. I'm bored here — no fights, no decent mead. My longship left without me.
DLG_YARYY_FIGHT: There'll be plenty of fighting. Coming with us?
DLG_YARYY_MEAD: Then promise a fight at least! They say outlaws roam the woods.
DLG_YARYY_JOINED: Now that's talking! My axe has been bored too long.
DLG_PRIEST_HELLO: Peace be with you. I'm going to Polotsk, to Holy Sophia, but these woods frighten me alone.
DLG_PRIEST_EVIL: They say a midday spirit walks the graveyard, and a restless dead man with her. The old faith is strong here — the demons are glad of it.
DLG_PRIEST_JOINED: God bless you. I'll bind your wounds, and with God's help we'll drive off the unclean.
